inspection_summary: Inspected all 576 normalized lines. The source develops an explicit chain from a zero-free region and verified RH height to Chebyshev-function error bounds, transfers those bounds to pi(x)-li(x), and applies them through analytic-to-finite verification bridges. Fifteen materially distinct readable semantic units were accepted without a quota. The exact P-integer exclusion calculation at lines 419-451 remains meaningful but is quarantined because its central displayed definitions and summation criterion are not safe to reconstruct from the extracted formula layout.

accepted_units.title: Trading verified RH height and a zero-free region for an effective constant
accepted_units.why_material: The text fixes the auxiliary scale parameter, combines Kadiri's zero-free region above a threshold with the verified zero height below it, solves the matching condition, and obtains a region usable by Schoenfeld's explicit-error machinery. This is a reusable local-to-global certification pattern rather than a bare constant update.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 61-66 explicitly limit the construction: it preserves B=17 to reuse Schoenfeld's numerical work rather than optimize the general two-parameter region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent. The inequalities and matching equation are readable in the text layer, but radicals, absolute-value bars, and exponent placement require scan verification before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Extending explicit theta and psi error bounds across analytic and finite ranges
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 gives explicit bounds, then the proof transports Schoenfeld's large-range argument to the new constant, uses independent psi bounds plus the psi-theta discrepancy on intermediate ranges, exploits the shape of epsilon on the small range, and reduces the final bounded residue to computation.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is a layered coverage argument: large x by modified zero-free-region analysis, medium x by tabulated bounds, small x by coarse Chebyshev inequalities, and x at most 599 by direct verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent. The prose fixes the logical range decomposition, while displayed radicals, negative exponents, and decimal scientific notation should be scan-checked before exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Transferring theta error to pi(x)-li(x) by partial summation
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies the integral identity that converts control of theta(x)-x into control of pi(x)-li(x), separating an endpoint term, an integrated error term, and constants. This is the conceptual bridge on which Theorem 2 rests.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited Dusart and Ford bounds are comparison context; the source-local mechanism is equation (8) and the observation that better theta control propagates through it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multi-line integral display has text-layer reading-order risk. Its qualitative decomposition is supported by adjacent prose, but exact signs, limits, and denominators require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Splitting the partial-summation integral into a finite prefix and a controlled tail
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2's proof chooses a split point, dominates the tail using Theorem 1 and a derivative majorant, and rewrites the finite prefix by interchanging summation and integration. The combination isolates all difficult asymptotic dependence in a monotone majorant while leaving a finite explicit remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivative comparison requires alpha below 7/4 and selects 7/5; the finite-prefix identity also imports theta(t)<t below 10^8.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent. In particular, the summation-integral display at lines 203-208 is scrambled in extraction; accept the prose-supported strategy, but scan-verify the exact identity and all exponents before symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: Closing an analytic bound with breakpoint maxima and finite verification
accepted_units.why_material: A chosen split point yields a uniform large-range bound, while the known sign of pi(x)-li(x) below 10^14 reduces interval maxima to prime breakpoints. Checking those breakpoints extends the estimate down to the stated threshold.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument depends on the imported sign result and reports a Mathematica computation; it is computational evidence, not a source-contained formal verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The breakpoint formula and exponents are readable but formula-dependent; exact numerical reuse should be checked against the page image or retained computation.

accepted_units.title: Propagating an improved prime-interval estimate into an arithmetic-progression threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The source shows how an explicit prime in [k,k+a] estimate can be substituted into an existing combinatorial proof to lower the classification threshold for maximally intersecting arithmetic progressions. It also distinguishes analytic improvement from the remaining infeasible direct-computation barrier.
accepted_units.context_note: The combinatorial lemmas and most of the proof live in Ford's cited work, so this unit records a source-grounded transfer interface rather than a self-contained derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition and conclusion are prose-readable; the displayed expression for a and the replaced comparison formula have split radical/exponent layout and require scan verification for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Reducing a short-interval prime theorem to a uniform theta-error lemma
accepted_units.why_material: The corollary states the target multiplicative interval, and Lemma 1 supplies the precise theta-error scale needed to make the theta increment positive. This cleanly exposes the analytic subgoal behind the prime-existence claim.
accepted_units.context_note: The threshold in the corollary is ultimately lower than the initial analytic range only after the later finite-gap descent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; fraction baselines and powers of log are visibly displaced in extraction, so the exact interval and lemma constants require scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Piecewise endpoint certification of a uniform theta-error bound
accepted_units.why_material: The proof combines a psi bound with an explicit psi-theta discrepancy, defines a normalized error expression, and certifies it on exponential intervals using a bound at each left endpoint and evaluation at the right endpoint. A finite table covers the middle range and Theorem 1 covers the tail.
accepted_units.context_note: The author notes that a finer interval grid could improve the coefficient, but stops because the available source table lacks the desired intermediate entry and the present constant suffices.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula- and table-dependent. The interval endpoints and reported maxima are readable, but equation (13), scientific-notation exponents, and column alignment require scan verification before exact computation.

accepted_units.title: Positive theta increment certifies a prime in the target interval
accepted_units.why_material: The source converts the theta-error lemma into prime existence by showing the Chebyshev-function increment over the target multiplicative interval is positive. This is the central semantic bridge from an analytic error estimate to a discrete existence conclusion.
accepted_units.context_note: At this stage the argument applies only for x at least e^35; the remaining lines construct a separate descent to smaller x.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The implication is prose-supported, but the displayed increment and constant inequality are formula-dependent and should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrapping short-interval coverage downward with maximal prime gaps
accepted_units.why_material: A certified maximal gap up to a high cutoff yields a lower threshold through a simple inequality; recomputing a smaller maximal gap below that threshold permits repeated descent until exhaustive search is cheap. This is a reusable analytic-to-finite bootstrapping pattern.
accepted_units.context_note: The first gap certificate is cited, later gaps and the final exhaustive search are reported computations, and neither constitutes an independently reproduced verification here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The recurrence logic is clear in prose. Equation (14), powers, and scientific-notation thresholds require scan or computation-log verification for exact numerical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Sensitivity analysis for improving the short-interval result
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies the theta-error coefficient, rather than a farther maximal-gap computation, as the effective bottleneck, quantifies how a smaller coefficient changes the interval constant, and compares a differently shaped known interval result.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed use for primes between cubes is only a cited prospective application, not demonstrated in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-dependent; exact comparison thresholds and interval notation should be scan-checked because of superscript and inverse-symbol layout.

accepted_units.title: P-integers and the route from prime-counting error to a finite upper bound
accepted_units.why_material: The text defines the residue-system property, gives contrasting examples, states earlier bounds, and explains that replacing an older pi(x)-li(x) estimate by Theorem 2 improves the upper bound. This exposes the semantic dependency of the application without relying on the damaged subsequent formulas.
accepted_units.context_note: The actual exclusion criterion and its numerical verification occur in lines 419-451 and are quarantined pending scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition and examples are readable. Concrete residue sets are illustrative execution details; the exact exponent formatting in prior and improved bounds should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Why optimizing secondary asymptotic coefficients barely moves the P-integer threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains the origin of two coefficients as approximations to asymptotic expansion coefficients, tests their unattainably ideal replacement, and finds negligible improvement. It thereby isolates the main theorem, or a different approach, as the consequential lever.
accepted_units.context_note: The final cited announcement of a proof is external evidence and is not treated as a proof in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The qualitative sensitivity conclusion is explicit in prose; the displayed asymptotic expansion has extraction-layout risk and needs scan verification for exact term placement.

accepted_units.title: One explicit estimate yields sharply different Ramanujan-inequality thresholds with and without RH
accepted_units.why_material: The source records the same target inequality under two regimes: verified computation plus an RH assumption gives a much smaller threshold, whereas the unconditional use of the explicit estimate produces an exponential threshold. The contrast illustrates how assumptions and explicit-error strength control downstream usability.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivations are in cited work, so this is an application comparison rather than a source-contained proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose thresholds are readable, but the displayed Ramanujan inequality has fraction and argument-placement risk and should be verified against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Four non-equivalent levers for sharpening the explicit-error method
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion separates raising the verified RH height, strengthening the zero-free region's constants, feeding both advances into independent psi estimates, and rebuilding Schoenfeld's argument for the target parameters. This is a source-specific map of where improvement can enter and notes that verified height alone has only mild influence.
accepted_units.context_note: These are proposed directions, not observed improvements in this source.
